text: Hey, it's me the striper report guy with your northeast offshore fishing rundown for the week of September 2nd, 2026. Let's start from the south and get into it. Since last week the canyons off Maryland and Virginia have given up good numbers of Mahi and white marlin as well as the occasional yellowfin. A little closer to Ocean City there are Mahi all over the pots and some nice midshore wahoo being trolled up on the backside of the full moon. Moving on up the coast, if it's yellowfin you're after take a poke to Tom's Canyon. There have been a good deal of yellows, big eyes and swords caught that way over the past week. In the shipping lanes off New Jersey and western Long Island there are scant bluefin while the bite toward Coimbra and the Bacardi has rebounded quite a bit. You've also got some yellowfin in the mix since the full moon. Some days they're showing up in force, other days it's a tough pick. Find the porpoises, skipjacks or slicks and chicks and hook some poppers before setting up the jig. South of Block and the Elizabeth Islands there aren't many wreck size fish. It's mostly giants being pulled off the draggers. Meanwhile, east of Cape Cod the wreck bite has been on and off but the commercial guys are getting shots at their giants as well. Further north from Stellwagen to Jeffries you have a few wreck bluefin here and there but the big news this week coming out of New England is the 500 lb state record swordfish caught within 10 mi of the coast of Maine. For the full northeast offshore report visit the OnTheWater YouTube channel every Wednesday at 5:00 p.m. Have a great week guys. Go get them.
